subject.title: [Security] Insecure storage of GitHub PATs in plain text during OAuth flow

question: Should OpenClaw extend its security boundary to encrypt rotating OAuth credentials at rest, and if so which cross-platform key-custody and compatibility model should become the canonical auth-profile contract?
rationale: Current documentation intentionally treats OAuth credentials as plaintext residuals protected by file permissions and OS isolation; changing that boundary affects every OAuth provider, upgrades, headless deployments, recovery, and runtime token rotation.

options.title: Generic secure credential store
options.body: Create a provider-neutral rotating-credential store with OS-backed or explicitly configured key custody plus doctor migration and compatibility tests.

options.title: Harden existing plaintext boundary
options.body: Retain plaintext auth profiles but strengthen permission enforcement, diagnostics, documentation, and threat-model guidance.

options.title: Require external credential proxy
options.body: Move rotating OAuth custody out of OpenClaw and require a documented external credential service for hardened deployments.

recommendation.title: Generic secure credential store
recommendation.body: Create a provider-neutral rotating-credential store with OS-backed or explicitly configured key custody plus doctor migration and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent SecretRef hardening work most directly defines the current credential-storage boundary that this decision would extend.
